newsitem.title: USA: IRS issues final rules for private-activity bonds.
newsitem.headline: IRS issues final rules for private-activity bonds.

text.p: U.S. Internal Revenue Service issued long-awaited final regulations that tell state and local governments when their debt will be treated by the Service as a financing of "private activity."

Originally proposed in December 1994, the rules offer detailed guidance for a provision in the Tax Reform Act of 1986 that says that no more than 10 percent of a public-purpose tax-eempt bond issue can benefit private business.

Originally proposed in December 1994, the rules offer detailed guidance for a provision in the Tax Reform Act of 1986 that says that no more than 10 percent of a public-purpose tax-exempt bond issue can benefit private business.
IRS said in its 139-page rule package, which will appear in the Federal Register shortly, that the new standards will take effect May 16.
Also, IRS issued two briefer rules, called "revenue procedures," that are expected to be of interest to colleges, medical facilities and other such issuers of tax-exempt bonds.
The rulings tell bond issuers under what circumstances they can have research agreements or management contracts with private entities without threatening the tax-exempt status of their bonds.
The two rulings also take effect May 16.
Catherine Spain, chief lobbyist for the Government Finance Officers Association, said she had not yet see the final private activity bond rules.
But she said she is disturbed that IRS did not follow the group's advice last year and reissue the complicated standards in proposed form for further comments.
Spain said that the May 16 effective date gives municipalities plenty of time to seek some IRS finetuning of the final rules, if necessary.
But if issuers decide major changes are needed in the standards, they will have no alternative but to go to the U.S. Congress for help, Spain said.
